candidate: warp-per-head decode attention with a shuffle-exact 256-lane tree, selected for head_dim == 512
reason: bit-exact against the block kernel and 28% faster on the full-layer geometry (851-870 us vs 1186 us at keys=1024), which moved the campaign metric to 24.6025 tok/s from 23.1517 (+6.3%) with no regression on any other primary row

mechanism.before: the 256-lane tree spans eight warps, so every key costs a shared-memory partial row, three LDS tree rounds, a publish/broadcast pair and a barrier sequence; iteration 20's ablations showed the per-key cost is invariant to the work inside the key iteration, which localizes it to that cross-warp machinery
mechanism.after: warp lane w owns tree lanes [8w, 8w+8), so the block kernel's strides 128/64/32/16/8 become shuffle lane distances 16/8/4/2/1 and its strides 4/2/1 become in-lane adds: five shuffles plus three adds per key with no LDS traffic and no barriers inside the key walk
mechanism.exactness_argument: same pairs in the same order - pass 1's dot tree, pass 2's per-lane key partition (tree lane L accumulates keys j == L mod 256 ascending) and pass 3's per-dimension ascending-j chains are all preserved, so every logit and the denominator are bit-identical
mechanism.why_only_head_dim_512: one warp per (token, head) is 16 warps for a decode step against the block kernel's 128; at head_dim 256 the warp kernel measures 822 us against the block kernel's 652-700 us, so the launcher keeps the block kernel there and takes the measured win only where it exists

correctness.contract: bit-exact with the block kernel (same-schedule arithmetic), not a changed-arithmetic candidate: no production-profile KL gate applies
correctness.parity_result: bitwise equal on every shape, both dtypes, keep and holes masks
correctness.routing_test: tests/test_gpu_gemma4_attention_decode_parity.py::test_decode_variant_selection_is_by_geometry - asserts head_dim 512 -> warp, 256/128/768 -> block through hipengine_gemma4_attention_decode_variant(), so the intended kernel is confirmed rather than inferred from timing
correctness.public_path_parity: true on all four re-measured campaign rows (instrumented ids == untouched LLM.generate() ids)

microbench.protocol: one launch per measurement window, 30 iterations, same clock state for each A/B pair, device sync at the end
microbench.clock_caveat: the same sliding/1024 case measures 652 us at 40 iterations and 486 us at 400, so absolute microbenchmark numbers depend on the clock state; every A/B here compares runs at the same iteration count back to back

campaign_rows.regression_check: decode improved on all four rows, prefill is within run-to-run noise on all four, public wall time improved on all four; no confirmed regression

grid_scaling.reading: 16x the work costs 1.6x the time: the machine is far from throughput-bound, so the block kernel's remaining cost is per-block latency, not bandwidth or issue rate
